channel.title: Said & Checked: Housing and Communities — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Housing and Communities, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Housing and Communities, 2026-11-20: 1 contradicted (David Schweikert)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • David Schweikert, U.S. Representative: “interest rates on a 30-year mortgage yesterday hit 7.5 percent” Contradicted. Freddie Mac's weekly survey put the 30-year fixed rate at 7.28% for the week ending Nov. 19, 2026 and 7.11% a week earlier, and AskAmerica's FRED data show no weekly reading at 7.5% this fall. What remains open is a daily index, which was not read and can differ from the weekly survey.

item.title: Said & Checked, Housing and Communities, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Bruce Westerman, Eric Schmitt)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Bruce Westerman, U.S. Representative from Arkansas: “Originally, the Tribe's reservation spanned over 15,000 acres until the city of San Diego initiated a land sale in 1931 so it could build the El Capitan Reservoir.” Unsettled. The Capitan Grande Reservation covered 15,753 acres, which matches 'over 15,000 acres', and the El Capitan Reservoir flooded its core in 1931 (as compiled by Wikipedia). A summary of a UC Irvine article cites purchase acts of 1919 and 1932, so the year the sale began is not confirmed.
  • Bruce Westerman, U.S. Representative from Arkansas: “The Pit River Tribe, which was federally recognized in 1976, consists of 11 different California Tribal bands and resides on a 100-square-mile reservation.” Unsettled. The 1976 federal recognition and the 11 bands match the tribe's site and Wikipedia's account. The tribe's site describes 'the 100 Mile Square' as its ancestral territory, and Wikipedia lists its trust land (six rancherias and the XL Ranch) at about 9,500 acres. No primary record of current reservation area was read, so the 100-square-mile figure is not settled.
  • Eric Schmitt, U.S. Senator from Missouri: “this would authorize the National Park Service's ability to enter into a defined agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to manage, market, and execute private events at Gateway Arch National Park.” Unsettled. Section 3(a) of H.R. 5254 (Senate-reported text) lets the Interior Secretary enter a one-time agreement of up to five years with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation 'to host private events at the Park'; AskAmerica's CRS bill summary matches. The text says 'host' and does not mention managing or marketing events, so whether it covers those is a reading.
